objective: Bind the ETF pair relative-strength switch candidate family to verified source cards before handing the 18-candidate batch (12 PAIR + 6 STATIC5050 placebo) to the screening lane for K1/K2 testing against S3, resolving reports/research/harvest/directions.jsonl's dir:etf_pair_relative_strength_switch and the relative_value.pairs_stat_arb coverage-map gap's long-only leg.

sources.core_claim: QuantConnect forum rule: 20-day relative momentum switch between QQQ and SPY, +1.0% QQQ bias, 0.5% switch threshold, 5-day rebalance. Reported 2010-2024 backtest: CAGR 19.02%, Sharpe ~0.8, MDD ~30%. Platform staff flagged real code bugs in the same thread; no post-fix numbers, no independent replication, no OOS/live record.
sources.project_applicability: Grounds the binary relative-strength-switch mechanism and the QQQ/SPY pair specifically; this batch tests the mechanism fresh via rotation_cell (63/126-day lookback, monthly rebalance) plus five extension pairs, not this source's own parameters or numbers.
sources.reflection: Rule and parameters are rotation_cell's own already-live, unedited mechanism at menu size 2, not fit to this batch's return data; the only new degrees of freedom are the pair (ticker pair) and the lookback (63 or 126, a small preregistered bounded sweep within the 24-candidate lightweight-exemption budget), not tuned to any window's outcome.

sources.core_claim: Dual-momentum/relative-strength rotation strategies suffer whipsaw losses in choppy markets (2015 example: -6.2% despite flat global equities) and lag V-shaped recoveries (2009 example: 11.8% vs 32.7% buy-and-hold).
sources.project_applicability: Negative-evidence check for the pair-switch mechanism family; names the exact failure mode (whipsaw, recovery lag) the stress window and the STATIC5050 placebo are designed to catch.
sources.reflection: General commentary retrieved via WebSearch snippet, not specific to any of the six pairs; used to motivate the preregistered STATIC5050 counter-evidence check, not to set any parameter.

sources.core_claim: Jegadeesh & Titman (1993), 'Returns to Buying Winners and Selling Losers': the foundational academic paper documenting cross-sectional relative-strength/momentum -- ranking assets by trailing 3-12 month returns and holding the winners predicts continued outperformance over the following 3-12 months, the academic basis for the relative-strength-switch mechanism this batch's PAIR candidates implement between two names instead of a broad cross-section.
sources.project_applicability: Foundational academic grounding for the relative-strength ranking mechanism (rank by trailing return, hold the stronger performer) that both `rotation_cell` generally and this batch's 2-name pair switch specifically implement; not re-fetched this session (background knowledge, well-established finance literature), no parameter is copied from its specific US-stock 1965-1989 sample.
sources.reflection: Long-established, heavily replicated finding; not used for any specific numeric parameter, only for the mechanism's academic basis. This batch's own lookback grid (63/126 trading days ~= 3/6 months) and pair selection are its own choices, tested fresh against K1/K2 rather than assumed from the 1993 sample.
